newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn adopts steps to rein in year-end spending.
newsitem.headline: Bonn adopts steps to rein in year-end spending.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet adopted on Wednesday measures aimed at cutting costs by curbing government agencies' year-end spending binges.

The plan by Finance Minister Theo Waigel will give ministries and other government bodies greater discretion over spending and revenues to discourage them from their practice of draining accounts at year-end to ward off budget cuts.
Germany, under pressure to rein in its budget deficit to qualify for European monetary union (EMU) is trying everything it can to stamp out wasteful spending.

Under the new measures, outlined in a cabinet statement and due to be implemented starting with the 1998 budget, government bodies will be able to carry over unspent funds to the following year, which previously they could only do with multi-year appropriations.
Waigel will not, however, abandon the principle of annual budgets, which he said is part of the foundation of the economy and financial markets.
Government bodies will also assume greater powers over their revenues, and cost-benefit analysis will be introduced in public administration.
Waigel will also employ more auditors in the government accounting office to review budgets.
